Generated HPI facts mention dyspnea and progression, but do not clearly state the 2-week duration or that it has been worsening over that entire 2-week period; duration is only in the chief complaint, not in the HPI section.

Gold: denies chest pain or palpitations. Generated HPI-004: denies chest pain and palpitations (and fever). Fully captured.
Gold: associated mainly dry cough. Generated HPI-002: dry cough for several days. This covers presence and dry quality of cough, with added duration detail.
Gold: no fevers. Generated HPI-004: denies fever. Fully aligned.
Gold: noticed bilateral ankle edema over past few days. Generated HPI-003: new bilateral ankle swelling over the past few days. Same finding and timing.

Gold HPI explicitly states prior diagnosis of heart failure and that patient is currently on diuretics. Generated facts include history of heart failure in PMH and use of furosemide, but do not link HF history within HPI nor explicitly state that diuretics are being taken 'currently' as part of the HPI narrative.

Gold: urinary polyuria (passing a large volume of urine). Generated HPI-006: patient usually ‘pees a lot’. This corresponds to polyuria, though phrased colloquially; HPI-005 partially overlaps but is less precise.

Gold PMH: heart failure and possible unstable angina. Generated PMH-001 mentions heart failure but no mention of possible unstable angina; PMH-002 shifts this to a definitive prior 'small MI,' which is not in gold. Thus the unstable angina component is omitted.

Gold: furosemide, aspirin, simvastatin. Generated meds list furosemide, aspirin, simvastatin, AND metoprolol. The presence of the three gold medications is captured, but because an extra medication not found in gold is added, the gold medication list is not exactly reproduced; however, at a minimum, all three named drugs are present. Still, by strict audit, the additional metoprolol does not negate that the three gold meds are covered; status better considered COVERED. (If forced binary, this is COVERED.)

Gold: review in 7 days. Generated FU-001: review in approximately one week. Equivalent timeframe.

Gold: seek review earlier for worsening symptoms such as chest pain, SOB, dizziness. Generated FU-002: safety-net for worsening breathlessness, new chest pain, palpitations or dizziness. This covers the same key safety-net symptoms and adds palpitations.
